text:
mira: Hey team — onboarding check: we brought up 13B 4-bit quantized on A100-80GB-equivalent SKUs across AWS/GCP/Azure. Observed consistent p50 (~1.2ms/token) but Azure p95 is ~30% higher than AWS/GCP. Anyone seen this before?

alex: Which driver/CUDA stacks are you running? Azure images sometimes ship newer drivers that change kernel selection.

mira: Quick summary:
``nAWS: driver 535.86, CUDA 12.1
GCP: driver 535.86, CUDA 12.1
Azure: driver 535.113, CUDA 12.2
```
p50 ~1.2ms across, p95: AWS/GCP ~1.6ms, Azure ~2.1ms. Throughput similar though — tails are worse on Azure.

jordan: Sounds like a kernel fallback or cublas heuristic difference. Can you run a cublas matmul microbench or NVIDIA Nsight Compute to confirm which kernel variant is picked at 2k context length?

mira: Kicked off ncu. Preliminary matmul bench shows Azure picking an fp16 GEMM path with extra reductions instead of the fused/wider kernel we see on AWS/GCP.

ravi: Also check clock governance and power/thermal defaults. `nvidia-smi -q -d CLOCK` will show persistent clocks. If Azure nodes have lower persistent clocks it can blow up the tail under sustained load.

mira: Added clock/power outputs:
``nAzure: power limit 300W, persistent clocks: 1095/877, clock_delay: 0
GCP: power limit 350W, persistent clocks: 1410/1200
AWS: power limit 350W, persistent clocks: 1410/1200
```
So Azure is running lower clocks by default.

alex: That explains it. Lower clocks + different kernel = higher p95. Two mitigations: (1) force persistent high clocks for benchmarking/dedicated nodes; (2) pin the driver/CUDA in the Azure image (downgrade to 535.86 / CUDA12.1) and re-run.

mira: Ran a quick experiment: installed 535.86 on one Azure node and re-ran the workload — p95 dropped to ~1.65ms, close to AWS/GCP. Reproducible.

jordan: Nice. Action items for onboarding: (a) add an image validation step that runs a small matmul+kernel selection smoke suite and asserts kernel parity; (b) attach perf metadata (driver, CUDA, kernel names, persistent clock profile) to node records so the scheduler can route to matching stacks.

ravi: Agree. Also add runtime fallback policy: if p95 for a model in a region exceeds threshold, reroute to a region with a matching stack or to a compatible model variant to avoid user-visible regressions.

mira: Filed infra/eng-ml #4582 — "image perf validation + node perf metadata". Uploaded raw ncu CSV and perf chart to the internal artifact: https://internal.redwood/charts/1719000000-13b-4bit-azure-delta

alex: Please record kernel names and cublas/cublasLt versions in the eval artifact too. We previously missed a cublasLt heuristic change between driver versions that caused a regression.

mira: Will include kernel names and cublas versions in the eval artifact. Thanks! :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy 2024-05-09T15:22:17Z - azure-image-pin-535.86 started on ci-perf-02

ravi: Follow-up: can someone run the same workload with `--kv-cache-warmup` on and off and append the warmup vs cold runs to the chart? We want to rule out cold KV-cache interactions with clock governors.

mira: Running warmup variations now and will post updated chart (ETA ~20m).
